tagline: Thirty teams, 82 games, and the most talked-about athletes on social media.
why: The NBA is the world's top basketball league and probably the most global American sport, hugely popular across Asia. Its stars are celebrities on and off the court, and fans argue endlessly about who's the greatest, which trades make sense, and whether the league is better than it used to be. You can follow it casually through highlights, which come out during Hong Kong mornings.

essentials.title: League structure
essentials.body: 30 teams split into the Eastern and Western Conferences. Each plays 82 regular-season games from October to April.

essentials.title: The playoffs are what matters
essentials.body: Sixteen teams make the playoffs (with a 'play-in' for seeds 7 to 10). Every round is best-of-seven, ending in the NBA Finals in June. A ring (championship) defines legacies.

essentials.title: Stars move a lot
essentials.body: Unlike football clubs, NBA stars often switch teams through trades and free agency. Superteams and blockbuster trades are constant talking points.

essentials.title: Salary cap and the draft
essentials.body: A salary cap and luxury tax limit spending. The worst teams get the best chance at top picks in the annual draft, so bad teams sometimes 'tank' on purpose.

essentials.title: Stats rule the conversation
essentials.body: Points, rebounds and assists per game, plus shooting percentages. A 'triple-double' is 10 or more in three categories in one game.

essentials.title: The GOAT debate never ends
essentials.body: Michael Jordan vs LeBron James is the eternal argument. Knowing both sides is half of NBA small talk.

names.name: Michael Jordan
names.what: Won six titles with the Chicago Bulls in the 1990s, never losing a Finals. The default GOAT.

names.name: LeBron James
names.what: Four titles with three teams, the NBA's all-time leading scorer, and still playing past 40.

names.name: Stephen Curry
names.what: Golden State Warriors star who revolutionised the game with long-range three-point shooting. Four titles.

names.name: Kobe Bryant
names.what: Lakers legend with five titles, idolised across Asia. Died in a helicopter crash in 2020.

names.name: Nikola Jokić
names.what: Denver's Serbian centre, a three-time MVP and the best passing big man ever.

names.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
names.what: Oklahoma City Thunder guard, 2025 MVP and Finals MVP as the Thunder won the title.

names.name: Victor Wembanyama
names.what: San Antonio's 7-foot-4 French phenomenon who can do everything. 'Wemby'.

names.name: Luka Dončić
names.what: Slovenian star traded from Dallas to the Lakers in February 2025, one of the most shocking trades ever.

names.name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
names.what: Milwaukee's 'Greek Freak', a two-time MVP who won the 2021 title.

names.name: Kevin Durant
names.what: One of the best scorers ever, with two titles at Golden State.

names.name: Yao Ming
names.what: Chinese centre for the Houston Rockets and Hall of Famer, who made the NBA huge in China.

names.name: Los Angeles Lakers
names.what: Glamour franchise with 17 titles: Magic, Kareem, Shaq, Kobe, LeBron.

names.name: Boston Celtics
names.what: The Lakers' great rival, with a record 18 titles after winning in 2024.

names.name: Cooper Flagg
names.what: The 2025 number one draft pick, now in Dallas.

timeline.event: The league that becomes the NBA is founded.
Bill Russell's Celtics win 11 titles in 13 years.
Magic Johnson's Lakers vs Larry Bird's Celtics saves the league.
Jordan's Bulls win six titles. The Last Dance documentary covers this era.
The 'Dream Team' at the Barcelona Olympics makes basketball global.
Yao Ming is drafted first overall by Houston.
LeBron's 'The Decision' to join Miami creates the superteam era.
Curry's Warriors win three titles in four years with a three-point revolution.
LeBron's Cavaliers come back from 3-1 down to beat the 73-win Warriors.
Kobe Bryant dies; the season finishes in the Florida 'bubble'.
LeBron passes Kareem as the all-time leading scorer.
Luka is traded to the Lakers; Oklahoma City win the title.

now.headline: Lakers lead the West
now.detail: LA are 11-2, the league's best record, with Luka Dončić averaging about 38.6 points.

now.headline: Spurs right behind
now.detail: San Antonio are 10-2 with the best net rating; Lakers vs Spurs on 27 November is a big date.

now.headline: Celtics and 76ers set the East pace
now.detail: Boston (10-2) and Philadelphia (9-3) top the East; NBC's power rankings put the Sixers No. 1.

now.headline: Knicks are champs
now.detail: New York won the 2026 title over the Spurs in June, their first since 1973.

now.headline: Thunder hit by injuries
now.detail: OKC are 8-4 and in the play-in spot after injuries slowed them down.

now.headline: Giannis in Miami
now.detail: Antetokounmpo now plays for the Heat and is averaging 28.5 points.

local.headline: Morning viewing
local.detail: US games are on Hong Kong mornings, so fans watch at breakfast or on their commute. Highlights clips are how most people keep up.

local.headline: The NBA in Macau
local.detail: The NBA returned to China with preseason games in Macau in October 2025, its first games there since a political row in 2019.

local.headline: Kobe's legacy
local.detail: Kobe was hugely loved in Hong Kong and mainland China, and his jerseys and Nike shoes still sell.

local.headline: Street courts
local.detail: Courts in Southorn Playground (Wan Chai) and Kowloon parks are busy every night.

debates.question: Jordan or LeBron?
debates.sides: Jordan: six titles, never lost a Finals, unmatched aura. LeBron: longevity, all-round game, all-time scoring record.

debates.question: Is the regular season too long?
debates.sides: Load management and a lack of intensity make many say 82 games is too many.

debates.question: Is the league too reliant on three-pointers?
debates.sides: Some love the skill; others say every team plays the same way now.

debates.question: Are superteams bad for the league?
debates.sides: They create drama but make other teams feel hopeless.

sayThis.say: Curry changed how kids play the game.

avoid: Arguing GOAT with total certainty. It's a forever debate.
Calling the regular season meaningless to a fan of a team fighting for a spot.
Mixing up the Lakers and the Clippers, both in LA.
